speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: Largely, my speech will focus on reviewing and making necessary and reasonable changes to the current Vehicle Quota System (VQS), namely Category D of the Certificate of Entitlement, better known among Singaporeans in short as the COE.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: Additionally, I would also like to raise two other related proposals.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: The VQS was introduced and implemented in 1990 with the objective of regulating the growth of the vehicle population in Singapore.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: Under the current VQS, the COE are categorised into, A, B, C, D and E.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: Category C is for goods vehicle and buses.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: Category D is for motorcycles and Category E for all vehicles except motorcycles.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: I have brought up the issue of motorcycle’s COE multiple times in this Chamber in the form of Parliamentary Questions (PQs) and Committee of Supply (COS) cuts.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: This time around I am tabling this matter as an Adjournment Motion as I strongly feel that this issue needs to be conveyed, explained and discussed more in depth with the hope that MOT will consider reviewing motorcycle’s COE system which is Cat D.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: At this point, I would like to reiterate that the intention of calling for this review is mainly to benefit our fellow Singaporeans who depend on motorcycles to feed their family.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: According to MOM’s statistics for 2020, there were 220,000 residents who declared themselves as engaging in "own account work", that is, they are self-employed or freelancers.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: A number of these residents are likely to be motorcyclists engaged in delivery and dispatch services with one of the existing platforms.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: In addition, there are riders who are direct employees of various companies.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: There are no clear indicators on the number of Singaporeans who are riding commercially.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: When we take into consideration the road tax, insurance and other costs involved in purchasing a new bike, the number can go up to 14 months.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: More than a year of working just to afford a vehicle that is needed.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: A three-year-old motorcycle can go for around $10,000.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: A motorcycle with three years left on the COE can cost around $5,000.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: After buying a second-hand motorcycle, the new owner will soon be faced with a decision on whether to renew the COE when it expires.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: One month’s salary does not even cover the rental costs.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: And this is before we consider the cost of petrol, parking, ERP and more.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: The COE remains the largest cost factor in the purchasing of a motorcycle.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: In this regard, I am making a few proposals towards improving the COE system for Cat D.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: I am mindful that the ultimate goal is not to lead to an increase in the number of motorcycles on the road.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: Rather, my intention is to improve the well-being of our fellow Singaporeans who rely on riding motorcycles to make a living.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: I am reiterating my call for MOT to consider categorising the COE for motorcycles into classes according to engine capacity, similar to how the licences to ride motorcycles are categorised.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: This is a proposal I first mentioned in a cut I filed for the 2016 COS debates.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: I am also renewing my call for the number of COEs available for each category to be allocated in accordance with the percentage of these vehicles on our roads.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: Under the current practice, all motorcycles are grouped into a single Category D regardless of its engine capacity.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: When I raised this point in 2016, then Senior Minister of State for Transport Ng Chee Meng had replied, given that 70% of the motorcycle population in Singapore had an engine capacity below 200 cc, introducing such a differentiation would lead to rigidity and, subsequently, lead to higher volatility in the COE prices for motorcycles.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: This volatility has already set in as we can see from the COE prices for motorcycles, especially in the last few months.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: In this regard, I call upon MOT to consider my proposal towards making a proper and fairer allocation of quotas among the three different classes of motorcycles, according to the demand of the respective classes.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: This is to ensure that the cost of motorcycle ownership in this category is affordable for those who need it for income.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: In 2014, I filed a Parliamentary Question (PQ) asking if the COE for Class 2B motorcycles can be abolished and the reply was that the COE is needed to regulate the motorcycle population.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: I have thus refined my proposal to propose balloting as a substitute for the bidding process.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: I understand that in 2013, then Minister of State for Transport Josephine Teo had replied to a PQ about a balloting system for the COE for cars and said that it was not viable as it could encourage a black market.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: Mrs Teo also said that it was not possible to set a price for balloted COEs to deter speculators and yet remain feasible for genuine buyers.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: However, I believe that an introduction of a balloting system with conditions attached, similar to what is done for Build-To-Order (BTO) flats, could be a way to regulate the Class 2B motorcycle population.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: Like BTO buyers, prospective owners of Class 2B motorcycles are more likely to be first-time buyers with a genuine need.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: However, if MOT intends to retain the bidding system, I would like to ask the Ministry to consider allowing motorcycle buyers to bid for COE under their own name rather than through the dealership.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: This is to address the issue of possible speculation by dealers.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: LTA has maintained that there is no evidence of speculation.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: However, the number of expired or unused Category D COEs and the fact that the COE prices rose significantly in the May 2021 exercise despite the higher number of motorcycles COEs on offer, are signs that LTA may need to update its information.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: Next, Sir, I would like to propose that MOT consider allowing the extension or renewal of another five years for motorcycles whose COE was initially renewed for only five years, provided that the motorcycle is used primarily for the earning of income.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: The current practice is that a motorcycle's COE can be renewed either for (a) a continuous period of 10 years or (b) for five years only.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: However, if the COE is renewed for five years, it cannot be renewed for another five years upon the expiry of the first five years.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: I understand that this additional legislation is only available for Category C vehicles, that is, goods vehicles and buses, and is subject to the statutory lifespan for this class of vehicles currently set at 20 years.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: Given that there is a segment of our population that depends on their motorcycles for work, I am asking for the same flexibility offered to owners of goods vehicles and buses to be extended to the riders as well.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: In addition to the changes I am proposing to the COE system for Category D, I have two other proposals which I believe will benefit Singaporeans who rely on the motorcycle for work.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: First, I would like to reiterate my call for the Preferential Additional Registration Fee (PARF) rebate for motorcycles with Additional Registration Fee (ARF).

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: I note that then Minister for Transport Khaw Boon Wan had said that given the ARF for motorcycles are about 15% of the Open Market Value (OMV), the PARF rebate value would be too low to incentivise deregistration for motorcycle owners.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: But I am of the view that most motorcycle owners who choose to deregister their vehicles early would still value receiving the PARF rebate, given that most of them do not earn a high income.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: There should be also consistency in the payment of ARF and the PARF rebates for all vehicles.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: Most of the time, dispatch and delivery riders do not park at the prepared car parks at the area mentioned above because they will or might incur parking charges and also due to time factors, both of which will affect their earnings.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: In situations where they have been issued a fine for indiscriminate parking, it will further add into their expenses.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: Additionally, indiscriminate parking also poses a safety hazard for other road users.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: Having a designated area for dispatch and delivery riders to park their motorcycles would reduce incidences of indiscriminate parking, enhance the safety of pedestrians and other road users and is also time-saving for these riders.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: In short, an allocation of such an area will enhance the work routine and life circumstances for these riders.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: (In Malay):   Today, I would like to highlight the problems faced by Singaporeans who depend on motorcycles to support themselves and feed their families.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: In particular, I will concentrate on the Certificate of Entitlement system, better known as COE.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: In particular, I would propose several ways to improve the COE system for Category D, which is for motorcycles.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: I have questioned multiple times as well as given my opinions and proposals on the COE for motorcycles in this Chamber.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: I will highlight this again because the issue of motorcycle COEs involves as well as impacts motorcycle owners who need their vehicles to earn a living to support their lives and their families.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: Further, I suggest that the number of COEs available be allocated in accordance with the percentage of motorcycles on the roads in each category.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: In 2016, the Senior Minister of State for Transport at the time had replied that the move would lead to rigidity and further volatility in the COE prices for motorcycles.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: However, it is clear that the situation mentioned by the Senior Minister of State still happened recently in the current COE system.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: So, I hope that MOT will consider my suggestion so that we can create a fairer system for motorcyclists in Singapore.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: The second proposal is abolishing COE bidding for Class 2B motorcycles, that is, motorcycles which use engines below 200 cc, and replace them with a conditional balloting system.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: I understand that the then Minister of State for Transport had once replied to a question about balloting system for the COE for cars.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: She explained that such a system will cause problems like a black market and also mentioned the difficulty of determining a suitable price for the COEs.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: In my opinion, we should consider the creation of a system similar to the one used to purchase BTO flats.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: Those who wish to buy BTO flats and those who wish to buy Class 2B motorcycles are both definitely first-time buyers.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: If MOT does not wish to make changes to the existing bidding system, I would like to suggest that every possible buyer be allowed to participate in the bidding and not just rely on motorcycle dealerships.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: This move could reduce the negative effects caused by speculation on the part of the motorcycle dealers.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: Next, I would like to suggest a renewal or extension for COEs that had already been renewed for only five years, for motorcycles that are used primarily for work.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: Presently, such renewals or extensions are only offered for Category C vehicles, that is, goods vehicles and buses.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: Besides the COE, I would like to submit two more proposals.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: Since most of them who work as delivery workers do not earn a high income, any PARF rebates, even a modest amount, will be appreciated.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: More importantly, policies should be implemented consistently across all vehicles.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: Riders often avoid using the available parking lots because they want to save money and time.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: In situations where riders are fined for parking their motorcycles indiscriminately, those fines will further impact their livelihood.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: (In English): Sir, in conclusion, the Singapore Government has set targets for the number of vehicles on the road, including for motorcycles.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: Towards this end, policies such as the COE, the ARF, Electronic Road Pricing (ERP) and such, have been introduced and continuously refined towards this goal.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: At the same time, you must recognise there is a segment of our population that relies on motorcycles to make a living and they have been affected negatively by the impact of the policies.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: In my speech, I have proposed several refinements to existing policies; some of these are not new but they have been updated.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: I hope the Government will look into these proposals towards improving the conditions of our fellow Singaporeans who have had to endure challenging circumstances.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Besides Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap, various Members, including Mr Chong Kee Hiong, Mr Sitoh Yih Pin, Ms Joan Pereira and Mr Abdul Samad have raised similar concerns and offered various suggestions.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: We have also heard similar feedback from members of the public and the industry and have responded both in this House and through the media.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: In land-scarce Singapore, unfortunately, we do not have the luxury of letting everyone own private vehicles, be it cars or motorcycles.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: The COE system is a market-based mechanism that allows us to allocate limited resources efficiently.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: While it is not a perfect solution, the system has generally worked and COE prices fluctuate based on supply and demand, as should be the case.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: That said, we are mindful that motorcycle owners could have different needs from owners of other vehicle types.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: This is why there is a separate Category D for motorcycle buyers so that they need not compete with commercial vehicle and private car owners.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: So, unlike the other categories, Category D COEs do not contribute to Category E COEs, or the open category, which means that the quota of COEs is determined largely by the number of deregistered COEs in the preceding quarter.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: The high prices observed for motorcycle COEs of late indicate strong demand.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: It would indeed be a cause for concern if the COE prices are propped up because dealers are bidding for more COEs than they need and are not using them.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: However, we have observed very high utilisation rates over the past year, which suggests that the higher premiums are a result of higher demand.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Successful bidders of Category D COEs are issued temporary COEs or TCOEs, which need to be used to register motorcycles.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: These TCOEs will expire if they are not used by the bidders to purchase and register motorcycles within the six-month validity period and their bid deposits will be forfeited.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: These were the COEs that were secured in March 2021.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: We will continue to closely monitor the utilisation rate of TCOEs issued in recent months over the respective six-month validity period.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: This was because we returned the additional COE quota accumulated when bidding was suspended during circuit breaker from April to June 2020, together with the closure of vehicle showrooms.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Hence, it is important to assess whether the market-based COE system is working as intended or if there is some market failure.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: First, Mr Faisal suggested splitting the motorcycle COEs into sub-categories according to vehicle classes in the same manner as riding or driving licences, as well as allocate the COE supply for each category according to the percentage of these vehicles on our roads.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Former Member of Parliament, Mr Zainal Sapari had in 2015 suggested this as well as Mr Abdul Samad who just filed a Parliamentary Question for this Sitting.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Ms Joan Pereira had also spoken about separate quotas for motorcycles based on the different categorisation.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Mr Chong Kee Hiong also asked to create a new category of COEs for motorcycles used for delivery work.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: We have explained the considerations in the past and these considerations remain relevant today.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Unlike cars, the quota for motorcycle COEs is relatively small.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: For example, for August to October 2021, about 440 Cat D COEs were available in each bidding exercise.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: If we were to divide this further, there will be even smaller quotas for each sub-category.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: This will likely result in greater volatility and potential increases in COE prices.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Of note, allocating sub-category quotas based on the prevailing split in motorcycle population has its challenges.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: The percentage of Class 2B motorcycles registered fluctuates across the years and even from month to month.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: It would, therefore, be very difficult for us to arbitrarily select an allocation basis.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Second, Mr Faisal also suggested abolishing COEs for all Class 2B motorcycles and to replace it with a balloting system.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: I understand that the intent is to make COEs affordable for those who need a motorcycle for livelihoods but this is not necessarily better.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Such a two-tiered COE system is not equitable since other types of vehicles, such as cars and commercial vehicles, can also be used for livelihoods.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: More importantly, such a system requires us to arbitrarily set a price.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: If the price is too low, it will increase demand and crowd out those who truly need the motorcycle for a living and are prepared to pay a bit more for the value it brings.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Third, on allowing motorcycle buyers to bid for COE under their own name, this is already allowed as individuals can bid for COEs through the ATMs.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: However, many motorcycle buyers still choose to go through dealers as this will allow them to get their motorcycles immediately, using the TCOEs that the dealer has already secured.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Fourth, the five-year COE renewal option is something we created for vehicle owners who need their vehicles for only five years instead of 10 years.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: If we were to allow COEs to be renewed for five years repeatedly, there will be fewer COEs recycled for bidding.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: This would tilt the current balance between existing and prospective vehicle owners.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Fifth, on establishing a Preferential Additional Registration Fee (PARF) rebate for motorcycles, such suggestions to extend the PARF scheme for cars to other vehicles have been raised in this House before.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: The PARF system is intended to encourage early turnover of older vehicles and to keep our car population relatively young.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: PARF needs to be taken in totality with the significantly higher ARF on cars.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: We have already kept related costs for motorcycles lower.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: ERP rates for motorcycles are also generally half that of cars.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Last but not least, on the issue of parking.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: The parking provisions depend on the nature of the development and the geographical zone, including whether it is near public transport.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: We acknowledge that the food delivery sector has grown rapidly in recent years and that commercial developments have their own circumstances and needs as well.
